scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

P-M2C.name: meter-to-cash
steps: read collection (AMI interval read or field manual read)
estimate substitution when no accepted read

DA-MDMS.name: MDMS AMI read event log (system of record for AMI reads)

DA-RULES.name: billing import validation rule change log

M-DISPUTED-ACTUAL-READ-SHARE.name: Share of disputed bills built on an ACTUAL (vs ESTIMATED) read

M-TICKET-RESPONSE-P90.name: p90 dispute ticket response time vs SLA

F-01.statement: Among disputed bills, 1240 have read_type ESTIMATED and 1785 have read_type ACTUAL (billing-db).

F-02.statement: billing-db.tariff_change_log contains 0 records, i.e. no tariff changes are logged.

F-03.statement: Field route completion for manual-read accounts was 88% (vs a 95% target) over 9200 manual-read accounts for the period 2026-08..09 (route-log).

F-04.statement: CRM dispute ticket response times across 2440 tickets: median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, against an SLA of 3.0 days (crm-tickets).

F-05.statement: crm-tickets.dispute_volume_monthly: 610 disputes in 2026-06, 590 in 2026-07, 1180 in 2026-08, 1260 in 2026-09.

F-06.statement: Service contract §4.2 allows the utility to request route priority changes, which are executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

F-07.statement: route-log.lagging_routes returned 14 lagging routes, each with a distinct completion value; sample record shows route R-00 at 0.70 completion.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-RESPONSE-SPEED-GAP.statement: The dispute surge is primarily driven by slow or poor-quality ticket responses in CRM, not by actually incorrect bills, so an auto-answer agent would resolve it.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules (around August) is causing bills to be computed or accepted incorrectly, driving disputes.

H-AMI-MDMS-DATA-QUALITY.statement: Degraded AMI read delivery or MDMS validation (vendor side) is causing missing accepted reads, triggering estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE.statement: Manual field meter reading (contracted via MeterWorks) is failing or incomplete (missed/late routes), causing estimated or substituted bills.

H-SEASONAL-USAGE-SPIKE.statement: Bills issued since August are largely correct, reflecting a legitimate seasonal consumption increase, and the 'wrong bills' premise itself is unverified.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Of 3025 disputed bills, 1240 (41%) used an ESTIMATED read and 1785 (59%) used an ACTUAL read, so estimate substitution is not the dominant pattern behind disputed bills — most disputes involve bills built on an actual meter read, not a missing/substituted one.

Billing-db's tariff_change_log shows zero records, indicating no tariff/pricing changes occurred that could independently explain incorrect bills; this rules out a price-change explanation but does not bear on the AMI, field-read, import-rule, response-speed, or seasonal-usage hypotheses already in play.

Field route-log shows manual-read route completion of 88% against a 95% target for 9200 manual-read accounts over Aug-Sep, i.e. roughly 12% of manual-read accounts had incomplete/missed routes during the dispute-surge window. This is direct, authoritative evidence of a real (if modest) field-read collection gap, independent of AMI/MDMS, billing-rule, or CRM response-speed factors.

E-04.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL's stakeholder statement that there has been no tariff change this year corroborates the already-recorded authoritative finding (E-02) that no tariff change occurred since August; as an unverified stakeholder claim it adds no new authority but agrees with existing evidence and does not implicate any currently listed hypothesis.

CRM response-time data shows tickets are generally resolved well within SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days vs 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets), indicating response speed/quality is not the bottleneck behind the dispute surge.

crm-tickets.dispute_volume_monthly shows 610 (Jun) and 590 (Jul) tickets rising to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep), confirming a roughly 2x jump in dispute volume starting in August — this validates the magnitude/timing of the surge CL-01 describes but says nothing about why bills are wrong.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD, an interested party, claims a 3-reader staffing shortfall since July causes late routes and resulting estimated bills; this is an unverified mechanism offered for the route-completion gap already shown in E-03, not new authoritative data.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-08 (service contract §4.2) establishes that the utility may request route priority changes but that these are executed only after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD), formalizing the contractual basis for the existing K-DISPATCH human-approval constraint on push_route_update rather than revealing anything about the billing dispute causal chain.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: Route-log's lagging_routes query decomposes the aggregate 88% manual-read completion rate (E-03) into 14 individual routes, each with a distinct completion value (sample: route R-00 at 0.70); this is granular characterization of which routes are behind schedule, not an explanation of why they are behind.

U-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMA.question: Did billing import validation rules actually change around August, and if so which rule(s) changed and how do they mis-process actual-read bills?
U-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMA.decision_impact: Confirms or refutes the core causal mechanism; if no rule change is found, a different mechanism (not yet in the hypothesis set) must be investigated before any fix is built.
U-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMA.resolution_path: Query billing-config billing import validation rule change log (DA-RULES) for changes around August and correlate timing with the dispute surge (E-06).
U-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMA.safe_placeholder: Continue diagnostic data analysis only; do not build or deploy any automated bill-fix or auto-answer agent until the mechanism is confirmed.

U-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE-CAUS.question: Is the route-completion gap (E-03) actually caused by a 3-reader staffing shortfall since July (SH-FIELD's claim, E-07/CL-03) or by another cause?
U-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE-CAUS.decision_impact: Determines whether a staffing or dispatch remedy is relevant to the secondary route-completion gap, independent of the main billing-rule driver.
U-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE-CAUS.resolution_path: Correlate route-log completion data against MeterWorks staffing records (not yet available) rather than relying solely on SH-FIELD's unverified claim.
U-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE-CAUS.safe_placeholder: Do not push any route/dispatch changes based on the unverified staffing-shortage claim alone.

U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.question: Would AMI read-event records (currently inaccessible, mdms-export ACCESS_PENDING/DEGRADED) reveal any secondary AMI-side contributor to disputed bills if access were granted?
U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.decision_impact: Could qualify the rejected AMI/MDMS hypothesis if vendor access is later granted and data contradicts E-01's current conclusion.
U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.resolution_path: Wait for vendor-provisioned MDMS export access (recovery_decision log notes ACCESS_PENDING) then pull disputed/estimated read events.
U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.safe_placeholder: Treat AMI/MDMS as ruled out per E-01 for now; revisit only if vendor access is granted and new data contradicts this.

U-SEASONAL-USAGE-VALIDITY.question: Do a meaningful share of the 3025 disputed bills reflect genuinely higher seasonal consumption rather than billing computation errors?
U-SEASONAL-USAGE-VALIDITY.decision_impact: If a large share of disputes are legitimate consumption increases, the success metric (dispute volume to baseline) is partly the wrong target and a confirmed-error-rate metric is also needed.
U-SEASONAL-USAGE-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Compare disputed-bill consumption against prior-year same-period consumption per account in billing-db.
U-SEASONAL-USAGE-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Report both raw dispute volume and a confirmed-billing-error share; do not assume every dispute is a billing error.

A-DISPUTES-REFLECT-BILLING-ERR.statement: Rising dispute volume reflects actual billing errors rather than legitimate increased consumption, since H-SEASONAL-USAGE-SPIKE remains an unresolved candidate hypothesis.

A-RULE-CHANGE-MECHANISM.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August is the mechanism producing incorrect bills, though no billing-config rule-change-log evidence has yet been examined to confirm the change itself.

A-FIELD-GAP-SECONDARY.statement: The 88% manual-read route completion gap (E-03) is a real but secondary contributor, not the dominant driver, since disputed bills skew toward ACTUAL reads, not ESTIMATED (E-01).

G-1.statement: dispute volume back to pre-August baseline with correct bills

K-DISPATCH.description: Changes to field dispatch routes are executed only after runtime confirmation by the Field Operations Manager (service contract §4.2).

K-BILLWRITE.description: Writes to customer bills (re-bill, credit) require Billing Operations authority; no automated bill writes.

DA-PUSH-ROUTE-UPDATE.subject: ORG-FIELD
conditions: Requires Field Operations Manager confirmation at execution time per service contract §4.2 (E-08)

SC-ROOT-CAUSE-CONFIRMED.statement: The billing import validation rule-change log (DA-RULES) is reviewed and correlated with August dispute timing before any remediation is built.
SC-ROOT-CAUSE-CONFIRMED.threshold: billing-config rule-change log reviewed and correlation documented
SC-ROOT-CAUSE-CONFIRMED.validation_method: Query billing-config for rule changes around August and compare timing/impact against disputed ACTUAL-read bills (E-01).

SC-NO-AUTOMATED-BILL-WRITES.statement: No bill is adjusted or re-billed automatically without Billing Operations authority per K-BILLWRITE.
SC-NO-AUTOMATED-BILL-WRITES.validation_method: Audit action log: any write_bill_adjustment must carry a recorded SH-BILL Human Gate approval.

SC-DISPUTE-VOLUME-BASELINE.statement: Dispute ticket volume returns toward the pre-August baseline.
SC-DISPUTE-VOLUME-BASELINE.validation_method: Monitor crm-tickets.dispute_volume_monthly for 2+ consecutive months at/near baseline.

SC-ROUTE-COMPLETION-TARGET.statement: Manual-read route completion rate rises to the contracted 95% target.
SC-ROUTE-COMPLETION-TARGET.validation_method: Monitor route-log completion reports monthly after any field remediation.

VOB-R-2.unresolved_question: Is the manual-read route-completion gap (E-03, 88% vs. 95% target) actually caused by the claimed 3-reader staffing shortfall since July (E-07/CL-03, from SH-FIELD who has an incentive for headcount increase), or by another cause?
VOB-R-2.reason_deferred: proposed by reasoner R-17: The route-completion gap's cause is currently based only on an unverified, potentially biased stakeholder claim (E-07/CL-03); any eventual staffing/contract remedy (SR-R4) should rest on confirmed cause, not self-interested testimony.

ORG-FIELD contracted reader headcount records since July

problem_definition.requested_solution: SH-CS requests an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever causes wrong bills.
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1220-1260/month (Aug-Sep) (E-06).
59% of disputed bills (1785/3025) used an ACTUAL meter read rather than an ESTIMATED one, so estimate substitution is not the dominant pattern (E-01).
Manual-read route completion ran at 88% vs a 95% target over 9200 accounts Aug-Sep (E-03), a real but secondary field gap.
problem_definition.root_problem: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1220-1260/month (Aug-Sep) (E-06). With tariff changes ruled out (E-02) and ticket response times already within SLA (E-05), and 59% of disputed bills built on an ACTUAL meter read rather than an estimated one (E-01), the best-supported mechanism is a change to billing import validation rules around August that mis-processes bills based on actual reads, producing incorrect bills that drive the dispute surge (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE).

structural_remedies.description: Query billing-config's rule-change log (DA-RULES) and correlate any August-dated rule changes with the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills (DA-BILL/E-01) to confirm or reject H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.
structural_remedies.rationale: Read-only query against an AUTHORITATIVE source, no approval needed under K-BILLWRITE/K-DISPATCH, and 225 minutes remain; satisfies the SC-ROOT-CAUSE-CONFIRMED gating requirement.; residual gap: billing-config tool_health is UNKNOWN (untested), so the query may fail or return incomplete data; this step only confirms the mechanism, it does not fix anything.

structural_remedies.description: If R1 confirms a bad rule, correct/revert the specific billing import validation rule in billing-config so ACTUAL-read bills are processed correctly going forward.
structural_remedies.rationale: A configuration change to validation rules is not a 'write_bill_adjustment' under K-BILLWRITE and not a dispatch route change under K-DISPATCH, so no protected-action approval blocks it; contingent on R1 output within remaining budget.; residual gap: Exact rule and fix are unknown until R1 completes, so this remedy cannot be fully specified yet; it also does not correct bills already issued incorrectly.

structural_remedies.description: Route correction/re-bill of already-issued incorrect bills through SH-BILL's existing manual adjustment authority (K-BILLWRITE), rather than any automated write.
structural_remedies.rationale: This is exactly the existing authorized human-approval pathway (K-BILLWRITE, actor SH-BILL), requiring no new process or agent.; residual gap: Addresses downstream harm to affected customers, not the causal mechanism itself; scale of affected accounts is unknown without R1.

structural_remedies.description: Address the secondary route-completion gap (E-03) by increasing contracted manual-reader headcount with ORG-FIELD under the existing service contract, rather than automated route dispatch.
structural_remedies.rationale: Hiring/contract renegotiation with MeterWorks is procedurally consistent with K-DISPATCH/§4.2 (SH-FIELD confirmation) but realistically exceeds the 225-minute remaining contest budget.; residual gap: Route completion gap (M-ROUTE-COMPLETION-RATE, currently 0.88 vs 0.95 target) will likely persist through the contest window; the staffing-shortage cause itself (U-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE-CAUS) is still unverified beyond stakeholder claims E-07/CL-03.

decision_log.rationale: causal chain: Dispute ticket volume rose from ~600/month to ~1220-1260/month starting in August (E-06). → 59% of disputed bills are built on an ACTUAL read, not an ESTIMATED one, ruling out estimate-substitution (field-read failure, AMI/MDMS data quality) as the dominant driver (E-01). → No tariff change occurred since August that could independently explain incorrect bills (E-02). → Ticket response times are well within SLA, ruling out slow CRM response as the surge driver (E-05). → The remaining best-supported explanation is a change to billing import validation rules around August that mis-processes bills built on actual reads, producing incorrect bills that customers dispute (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE).; rejected framings: [('H-RESPONSE-SPEED-GAP', 'Contradicted by E-05: dispute tickets are resolved well within SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d), so slow response is not driving the surge.'), ('H-AMI-MDMS-DATA-QUALITY', 'Contradicted by E-01: most disputed bills (59%) are built on ACTUAL reads, not estimate-substituted ones, so degraded AMI/MDMS delivery is not the dominant driver.'), ('H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE', 'Although E-03 shows a real 88% vs 95% route-completion gap, E-01 contradicts it as the dominant dispute driver since most disputed bills use ACTUAL reads, not estimates.'), ('SH-CS requested solution (auto-answer + auto-fix agent)', 'Automated bill fixes are blocked by K-BILLWRITE pending Billing Operations authority, the causal mechanism is not yet confirmed via DA-RULES, and auto-answering would not help since response times already meet SLA (E-05).')]
